scdenney-open-science-skills-advisor.description: Consults Fable as an independent, read-only reviewer at an effort the caller matches to the question. The calling session (usually Opus, or Haiku) holds the task and escalates one decision point. Use before committing to an interpretation or a substantial piece of writing or analysis, when stuck or not converging, when changing approach, or as a final check on a finished task. Fallback for when the native advisor tool is unavailable. Not for a session already running Fable.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-advis.description: Consult an independent, read-only GPT-6 Astra advisor before committing to a substantive interpretation, approach, or final result. Not for routine work, implementation, or file edits. Uses gpt-6-astra at an effort matched to the question.

scdenney-open-science-skills-beamer.description: House rules and craft for LaTeX Beamer slide decks (lectures, seminars, talks), drawn from the author's own Overleaf edits and published slide-design guidance. Covers storyboarding, frame titles, slide prose, word and frame budgets, layout without overfull boxes, XeLaTeX fonts and Korean (xeCJK), color, figures and screenshots, Overleaf source hygiene, speaker notes, and a build-and-QA loop with a contact sheet. Use when writing, editing, reviewing, or building a Beamer deck, theme, or storyboard. A course skill supplies course facts and the frame skeleton; this skill supplies the craft. Not…
scdenney-open-science-skills-beamer.author: Steven Denney

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-beame.description: House rules and craft for LaTeX Beamer decks (storyboarding, slide prose, frame budgets, layout, XeLaTeX and Korean fonts, color, figures, Overleaf hygiene, build QA). Use to write, edit, review, or build a Beamer deck.
scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-beame.author: Steven Denney

scdenney-open-science-skills-citation-ch.description: Audits a manuscript's citations for fabricated or nonexistent sources, DOIs that resolve to a different work, mismatches between in-text citations and the reference list, APA 7 or journal style, and whether each source supports the claim it is attached to. Checks entries against Crossref, OpenAlex, and DataCite and labels anything it could not verify NOT CHECKED. Use to check citations, references, a .bib file, or DOIs, or when a source may be AI-invented. Figures and tables go to figure-table-audit.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-citat.description: Audit a manuscript's citations for fabricated sources, DOIs that resolve to the wrong work, in-text and reference-list mismatches, style, and claim support, verified against Crossref and OpenAlex. Use to check citations, references, a .bib file, or DOIs.

scdenney-open-science-skills-conjoint-cl.description: Turns a raw Qualtrics conjoint export into an analysis-ready long-format dataset, covering export settings, identifying the implementation, package or manual wide-to-long reshaping, choice-profile alignment, ratings, reference categories, pilot exclusion, and subgroup merges. Use when the user has a conjoint CSV to clean, reshape, or debug, cannot align choices with profiles, or asks what the data must look like before AMCE estimation. Design goes to conjoint-design, validity review to conjoint-diagnostics.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-conjo.description: Turns a raw Qualtrics conjoint export into analysis-ready long-format data: implementation identification, reshaping, choice-profile alignment, reference categories, and pilot exclusion. Use when a conjoint CSV needs cleaning, reshaping, or debugging before AMCE estimation.

scdenney-open-science-skills-conjoint-de.description: Designs conjoint and factorial-vignette experiments, covering attribute architecture and randomization restrictions, effective-N power, treatment realism, the choice among AMCE, marginal-mean, and AMIE estimands, forced-choice versus rating designs, and PAP tiers. Use when the user is planning a conjoint, drafting or critiquing an attribute table, asking how many respondents or tasks are needed, whether to report AMCEs or marginal means, or how to test interactions. Reviewing an existing design goes to conjoint-diagnostics, cleaning the export to conjoint-cleaning.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-conjo.description: Designs conjoint and factorial-vignette experiments: attributes and restrictions, effective-N power, estimand choice among AMCE, marginal means, and AMIE, forced choice versus rating, and PAP tiers. Use when planning a conjoint, critiquing an attribute table, sizing respondents and tasks, or testing interactions.

scdenney-open-science-skills-conjoint-di.description: Reviews an existing conjoint study for threats to inference and returns severity-ranked findings on design integrity, estimation, measurement error, external validity, and interpretation, including the guardrail against reading an AMCE as majority preference. Use when the user asks whether a conjoint design or analysis holds up, has referee comments on a conjoint, or wants a second opinion on estimation or interpretation. New designs go to conjoint-design, reshaping to conjoint-cleaning.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-conjo.description: Reviews an existing conjoint study for threats to inference and returns severity-ranked findings on design, estimation, measurement error, external validity, and interpretation. Use when checking whether a conjoint design or analysis holds up, or answering referee comments on one.

scdenney-open-science-skills-cross-natio.description: Designs multi-country survey experiments, covering case selection with a stated comparative logic, instrument localization and TRAPD translation, stimulus calibration, per-country power, and pooled versus per-country analysis with measurement-equivalence checks. Use when the user fields the same experiment in several countries, asks which countries to include, how to adapt an instrument without breaking comparability, whether to pool, or how large each country sample must be. Question wording goes to survey-design, reporting to methods-reporting, the study plan to pre-registration-writing.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-cross.description: Designs multi-country survey experiments: case selection, localization and TRAPD translation, stimulus calibration, per-country power, and pooled versus per-country analysis with measurement-equivalence checks. Use when fielding the same experiment in several countries.

scdenney-open-science-skills-deliverable.description: Turns raw captures (dictated braindumps in a deliverable's inbox/, or recent macwhspr dictation-log entries) into proposed planning-wiki changes, shown as one unified diff. Classifies each statement as a decision, evidence claim, question, task, or dropped item, traces it to its capture paragraph, tags unconfirmed names, numbers, and citations UNRESOLVED, and writes decisions only with the author's assent. Edits only the planning wiki, never source files. Use when asked to intake, absorb notes, or process the inbox, or after dictating notes from a talk, meeting, or reading session.
scdenney-open-science-skills-deliverable.tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-deliv.description: Turns dictated captures in a deliverable's inbox/ into a proposed planning-wiki diff, classifying and tracing each statement; decisions need the author's assent. Use to intake notes or process the inbox.

scdenney-open-science-skills-deliverable.description: Reviews a whole deliverable (talk, course module, paper, chapter, or referee report) against its manifest without rewriting it. Runs a deterministic gate for build, citations, numbers, facts, and leaks and stops on failure, then runs a finder over each section and a strong-model pass over the whole work, and adjudicates into checks/<date>/findings.json and report.md with anchored findings, severities, and honest NOT CHECKED coverage within a dollar budget. Use when asked to lint or review the whole talk, module, or paper, for a pre-ship review, or for the night shift. Revision stays serial…
scdenney-open-science-skills-deliverable.tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Agent

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-deliv.description: Reviews a whole deliverable against its manifest without rewriting it — deterministic gate, per-section finders, a whole-work pass, and adjudicated findings.json and report.md with honest coverage. Use before shipping a deliverable or for the night shift.

scdenney-open-science-skills-deliverable.description: Opens a deliverable (talk, course module, paper, book chapter, or referee report) for AI-assisted work across sessions. Interviews the author for the manifest, then scaffolds deliverable.yml, an append-only HANDOFF.md, a numbered planning/ wiki with open questions, an inbox/ for dictated braindumps, a gitignored checks/, and the house deck template for talks. Use when starting deadline-driven work that spans sessions, or when asked to open a deliverable, set up a talk, paper, or module for the pipeline, or make a manifest. Not for one-off tasks.
scdenney-open-science-skills-deliverable.tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-deliv.description: Opens a talk, module, paper, chapter, or referee report as a multi-session deliverable. Interviews the author, then scaffolds deliverable.yml, HANDOFF.md, the planning/ wiki, inbox/, and checks/. Use for deadline-driven work spanning sessions.

scdenney-open-science-skills-diverge.description: Generates 3-5 conceptually distinct approaches labeled Novel, Surprising, Diverse, or Conventional, and holds for the user's selection before implementing. The --codex mode runs the brainstorm on GPT-6 Astra via codex exec, then has Codex implement the selected approach. Use before committing to an approach when a creative, architectural, or analytical task has more than one non-obvious solution; use --codex when another model family should widen the range.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-diver.description: Generates 3-5 conceptually distinct approaches (Novel, Surprising, Diverse, Conventional) and holds for selection before implementing. Use before committing to an approach when a task has more than one non-obvious solution; --codex delegates the brainstorm to a fresh subagent.

scdenney-open-science-skills-doc-to-mark.description: Reads or converts documents in a research workflow, including PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, and CSV. Chooses direct reading or conversion, selects a converter from document structure, and decides whether the Markdown is tracked or temporary. Use when a document must be read, quoted, summarized, searched, extracted, or added to a source library. Scanned documents go to vlm-ocr and bulk intake to research-repo.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-doc-t.description: Read or convert documents (PDF, Office, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, CSV) in a research workflow: read directly or convert, pick the converter from document structure, and decide whether the Markdown is tracked or scratch. Use when a document must be read, quoted, summarized, searched, extracted, or added to a source library; scans go to $vlm-ocr.

scdenney-open-science-skills-fact-check.description: Checks whether each claim in a manuscript is supported by the source it cites, reading the project's per-source Markdown knowledge base. Flags contradicted, unsupported, overclaimed, out-of-scope, and misattributed claims with verbatim source quotes. Runs citation-check first, and stops at a pre-flight gate when the knowledge base is missing, incomplete, or holds unconverted PDFs. Use to verify that a draft's claims match the sources it cites.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-fact-.description: Fact-check manuscript claims against their cited sources in a per-source Markdown knowledge base. Use to audit claim support, overclaiming, direction, scope, and misattribution after source intake is complete.

scdenney-open-science-skills-figure-tabl.description: Runs end-stage QA on a finished figure and table set. Checks callouts, numbering, and cross-references, whether numbers in the text match the exhibits, self-contained captions and statistical notes, accessibility and production quality, and links to the SI and replication package. Values that could only be read off an image are marked for author verification rather than estimated. Use when preparing a submission. Design guidance during drafting belongs to figures and tables.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-figur.description: End-stage QA for a finished figure and table set (callouts, numbering, cross-references, text-to-exhibit consistency, captions and notes, accessibility, SI and replication linkage). Use when preparing a submission.

scdenney-open-science-skills-figures.description: Designs publication figures for social-science manuscripts. Covers chart choice, axes and scales, color and accessibility, legend order, captions that carry the title, and script-based reproducibility. Use when making, revising, or critiquing a figure for a paper, such as a coefficient plot, small multiples, a distribution, a trend, a map, or a network. Finished figure sets go to figure-table-audit for end-stage QA.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-figur.description: Design and format publication-quality figures. Use for chart choice, color, scales, legends, captions, accessibility, and reproducible figure workflows.

scdenney-open-science-skills-finished.description: End-of-session closure for a research or code repository. Records what changed into the project's own handoff and log files, separating verified work from work merely attempted, and reports what is left uncommitted. Use when wrapping up a session so the next one can resume without re-deriving state. Its start-of-session twin is sitrep.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-finis.description: End-of-session closure. Records what changed into the project's own handoff and log files, separating verified from attempted work, and reports what is uncommitted. Use when wrapping up a session. Twin of sitrep.

scdenney-open-science-skills-hypothesis-.description: Turns a theory into falsifiable, pre-registerable hypotheses, covering the DGP and DAG, identification, SATE versus PATE, counterfactual and directional framing, named estimands, justified SESOIs, the choice among NHST, equivalence, interval, and minimum-effect tests, scope conditions, and primary, secondary, and exploratory tiers. Use when the user asks to turn a research question or theory into hypotheses, whether a prediction is falsifiable, what the estimand is, or how to predict a null. Framing goes to narrative-building, the plan to pre-registration-writing.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-hypot.description: Turns a theory into falsifiable, pre-registerable hypotheses: DGP and DAG, identification, estimands, SESOIs, test choice among NHST, equivalence, and minimum-effect tests, scope conditions, and hypothesis tiers. Use when converting a research question into testable predictions or predicting a null.

scdenney-open-science-skills-journal-rev.description: Drafts a referee report for a journal editor. Produces a recommendation, claim-and-design summary, three to six decision-driving concerns, additional concerns, and a revision plan through five parallel adversarial finders, Breaker, Butcher, Shredder, Void, Situator, a Blue Team error filter, Chief Reviewer synthesis, Tone Guard legal pass, and optional confidential editor note. Use when the user has been asked to referee a manuscript. Self-audits go to paper-review-lite or presubmit, and author responses go to referee-response.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-journ.description: Draft a referee report on someone else's manuscript for a journal editor, using five adversarial finders, a Blue Team error filter, a Chief Reviewer synthesis, and a Tone Guard legal pass. Use when the user has been asked to referee a manuscript; self-audits go to paper-review-lite or presubmit, author responses to referee-response.

scdenney-open-science-skills-list-experi.description: Designs and diagnoses list experiments (the item count technique), covering whether indirect measurement is warranted, control-list construction against floor and ceiling effects, design variants, estimators and assumption tests in the list package, and power planning for the precision penalty. Use when the user measures a sensitive attitude or behavior and asks about list experiments, item count, unmatched count, or veiled questioning, or has an implausible prevalence estimate. Deciding whether sensitivity bias exists at all goes to survey-design.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-list-.description: Designs and diagnoses list experiments (the item count technique): whether indirect measurement is warranted, control-list construction, design variants, estimators and assumption tests in the list package, and power. Use when measuring a sensitive item or debugging an implausible prevalence estimate.

scdenney-open-science-skills-literature-.description: Builds or audits a literature review, producing an evidence map, the closest prior work, source clusters, a gap verdict, and a synthesis plan for the introduction. Use when the user asks whether a contribution is novel, who has studied a question, what the literature establishes, or how to organize a review, or wants a reading list, Zotero export, or pile of papers turned into one. For systematic reviews or meta-analyses it produces the protocol scaffold and routes registration (PROSPERO or OSF) and screening to dedicated tools.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-liter.description: Builds or audits a literature review: evidence map, closest prior work, gap verdict, and synthesis plan. Use to check whether a contribution is novel, map what a literature establishes, or organize a review; systematic reviews get a protocol scaffold.

scdenney-open-science-skills-llm-calibra.description: Reads model uncertainty from token log-probabilities. Covers collecting logprobs and aggregating multi-token labels, confidence tiers and margins for triage, calibration assessment with ECE, Brier scores, and reliability diagrams against human labels, responsible downstream use of confidence, and reproducibility archives. Use when the user asks about classifier confidence by item, logprobs, top-k tokens, calibration, ECE, Brier, reliability diagrams, or routing low-confidence cases to human review. Codebook and validation design go to text-classification.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-llm-c.description: Reads a model's own uncertainty from token log-probabilities: collecting and aggregating label logprobs, confidence tiers and margins for triage, calibration against human labels (ECE, Brier, reliability diagrams), downstream use, and reproducibility. Use for per-item classifier confidence or routing low-confidence cases to human review; codebook and validation design go to text-classification.

scdenney-open-science-skills-methods-rep.description: Audits a methods section against a 45-item reporting checklist synthesized from the APSA Experimental Section rubric, JARS-Quant, CONSORT, and DA-RT, covering pre-registration, recruitment, randomization and treatments, sample flow and attrition, sample-size justification, three-tier results labeling, conjoint reporting, validity, and open-science infrastructure. Use when checking whether a methods section reports enough, preparing a submission or replication archive, asking what CONSORT, JARS, or DA-RT require, or documenting a deviation from a pre-analysis plan. Writing that plan before…

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-metho.description: Audit a methods section against a 45-item checklist drawn from the APSA Experimental Section rubric, JARS-Quant, CONSORT, and DA-RT. Use before submission or archiving, or to document a pre-analysis-plan deviation.

scdenney-open-science-skills-model-commi.description: Runs a deliberative two-model committee of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus under a selectable chair, Fable by default, with `/model-committee-astra`, `/model-committee-opus`, and `/model-committee-sol` selecting the others. Use when a consequential decision has several defensible options and two model families should propose, critique, revise, and cross-rank them against a predeclared rubric before converging, as in research design, interpretation, architecture, manuscript strategy, or evaluation design. Not for factual lookups, independent-coder reliability, brainstorming, routine…

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-model.description: Run one consequential, contestable decision through a deliberative committee of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus, chaired by fable (default), astra, opus, or sol. Not for factual lookups, brainstorming, routine implementation, independent-coder reliability, or final professional judgment. Use when several options are defensible and the two model families should propose, critique, revise, and cross-rank under a predeclared rubric.

scdenney-open-science-skills-archive-cod.description: Runs several language models as independent coders on the same labeling or discovery task and reads their disagreement as data — panel assembly for model diversity, keeping votes independent, consensus rules, agreement statistics (Cohen's and Fleiss kappa, Krippendorff's alpha), the correlated-errors caveat that stops agreement being mistaken for validity, human validation beyond the panel, and reporting. Use when the user asks about a council, panel, ensemble, or jury of models, asks how to combine several models' labels, or asks what kappa or alpha to report for model coders. Single-model…

scdenney-open-science-skills-archive-cla.description: Runs several language models as independent coders on one labeling or discovery task and treats disagreement as data. Covers diverse panel assembly, independent voting, consensus rules, Cohen’s and Fleiss kappa, Krippendorff’s alpha, correlated-error limits on validity claims, human validation, and reporting. Use when the user asks about a council, panel, ensemble, or jury of models, how to combine model labels, or what kappa or alpha to report for model coders. Single-model codebook and validation work goes to text-classification, per-item confidence to llm-calibration-logprobs.

scdenney-open-science-skills-narrative-b.description: Drafts or audits a scientific paper’s introduction and framing — the real-world "why", an evidence audit, the funnel from theory to a falsifiable if-then with a named estimand, bridges across experiments, and a contribution list matched to the design. Use when the user asks to write, restructure, or critique an introduction, motivate or frame a paper, repair a gap-in-the-literature opening, sharpen or calibrate a contribution claim, or connect experiments into one argument. Sentence-level flow and wording are out of scope.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-narra.description: Drafts or audits a scientific paper's introduction: real-world motivation, evidence audit, theory-to-if-then funnel with a named estimand, bridges across experiments, and calibrated contributions. Use to write, frame, or critique an introduction.

scdenney-open-science-skills-orchestrate.description: Runs a multi-model orchestration workflow led by the session's Fable or Claude Opus model. Sends menial tool-calling work to Haiku subagents, judgment work to Opus subagents at an effort matched to each task, and high-stakes or fresh-perspective questions to a GPT-6 Astra Codex peer. Detects the lead from session context; `--lead fable` or `--lead opus` overrides. Use to orchestrate, delegate, fan out, get a decorrelated Codex opinion, run a blind Opus-Codex cross-check, or act as tech lead.
scdenney-open-science-skills-orchestrate.tools: Agent, Workflow, Bash, Read, Write, Edit

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-orche.description: Orchestrate complex work from an active gpt-6-astra or gpt-6.1-sol Codex session. The detected lead owns decomposition, integration, and verification; Astra keeps the hardest reasoning in the lead, while Sol escalates unusually difficult units to Astra. Both route bounded work to Sol at medium effort, mechanical work to Luna, and can use a cross-vendor Claude peer. Not for routine single-context work. Use when the user explicitly asks to orchestrate, delegate, fan out, parallelize, assign subagents, obtain independent checks, or have Codex act as tech lead.

scdenney-open-science-skills-paper-revie.description: Provides a pre-submission manuscript audit covering argument, numerical consistency, references and DOIs, writing, figures, CONSORT flow, pre-registration, and the replication archive. Use before paper submission or when a draft needs an adversarial, quote-grounded review with a journal-readiness checklist. Add `--codex` to run the specification independently on Claude and Codex, GPT-6 Astra, and cross-check findings.
scdenney-open-science-skills-paper-revie.tools: AskUserQuestion, Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch, Agent

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-paper.description: Run a pre-submission manuscript audit covering argument, numerics, references, writing, figures, methods, preregistration, and replication readiness. Add --codex for a cross-model pass in which Codex and Claude review independently and verify each other's findings.

scdenney-open-science-skills-paper-tex.description: Typesets a working paper or journal submission in house-style LaTeX from Markdown, Word (.docx), TeX, ODT, RTF, or HTML. Converts with pandoc, wraps the body in an EB Garamond template, builds the PDF with latexmk, and sets journal-specific spacing, page limits, anonymization, disclosures, and citation style. Use to format or convert a paper to LaTeX, make a working paper, or prepare a submission to a named journal.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-paper.description: Typeset a working paper or journal submission in house-style LaTeX from Markdown, Word, TeX, ODT, RTF, or HTML. Use to convert drafts, build PDFs, or prepare journal-specific spacing, limits, anonymization, disclosures, and citations.

scdenney-open-science-skills-pre-registr.description: Writes or reviews a pre-analysis plan before data collection — registry choice (OSF, AEA RCT Registry, AsPredicted, registered reports), PAP structure, models and decision rules locked in advance, analysis code run on simulated data, contingencies for attrition, failed manipulations, and exclusions, deviation records, and timeline. Operationalizes the pre-data-collection side of DA-RT. Use when the user asks to draft or audit a pre-registration or PAP, choose a registry, decide what to lock versus leave exploratory, or handle a later deviation. Hypotheses and estimands come from…

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-pre-r.description: Writes or reviews a pre-analysis plan before data collection: registry choice (OSF, AEA, AsPredicted, registered reports), locked models and decision rules, code run on simulated data, contingencies, and deviation records. Use when drafting or auditing a pre-registration or PAP, choosing a registry, or handling a deviation.

scdenney-open-science-skills-presubmit.description: Launches and configures the standalone presubmit CLI, an API-driven adversarial peer-review pipeline with 30-plus stages, including Red Team finders, Blue Team defence, verification cascade, legal pass, and copyedit, producing one consolidated report on disk. Verifies installation and API key, chooses the output location and smoke, standard, or custom mode, launches the run, and reports the result path. Use when the user asks to run presubmit, wants a deep unattended pre-submission audit, or needs a math or replication-code audit. Everyday self-audits go to paper-review-lite, and external…

scdenney-open-science-skills-qualtrics-o.description: Operates or audits a live Qualtrics survey through the v3 APIs without disrupting fielding. Covers publish gating, quotas, flow routing, embedded data, panel-vendor redirects, read-back verification, and a read-only pre-fielding audit. Use when publishing or patching a fielding instrument, when a quota counts without blocking, when configuring panel-vendor redirects or flow gates, or when auditing a survey before launch for consent gates, force-response completeness, quotas and redirects, anti-bot instrumentation, and language-arm symmetry.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-qualt.description: Operate or audit a live Qualtrics survey via the v3 APIs without breaking fielding: publish gating, quotas, flow routing, embedded data, panel-vendor redirects, read-back verification, and a read-only pre-fielding audit. Use when publishing or patching a fielding instrument, when a quota counts but never blocks, or before launch.

scdenney-open-science-skills-referee-res.description: Organizes an author’s response to peer review. Extracts every referee and editor point, tags severity and type, orders the revision by dependency, flags defensible pushbacks as questions, and builds a numbered comment → response → location letter whose substantive answers the author writes. Use when the user has referee reports, a revise-and-resubmit decision, or an editor’s letter and wants to plan the revision, draft the response letter, or check that every point was addressed. The reviewer-side twin is journal-review.
scdenney-open-science-skills-referee-res.tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-refer.description: Organize an author's response to peer review: extract every referee point, order the revision by dependency, flag possible pushbacks, and build the response-letter skeleton the author fills in. Use for revise-and-resubmit planning, response letters, or checking every point was answered.

scdenney-open-science-skills-replication.description: Scaffolds or audits a social-science replication package and evaluates the manuscript and archived research objects against FAIR principles. Scaffold mode writes the folder structure, README, master.R, figure-table crosswalk, codebook, LICENSE placeholder, and .gitignore; audit mode grades the package against a pre-release checklist and audits data, code, materials, identifiers, licenses, access restrictions, and availability statements. Use when setting up or repairing a package, checking one before submission, auditing FAIR compliance, or drafting availability statements. Adapted from…

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-repli.description: Scaffold or audit a social-science replication package, and audit the manuscript and archived research objects against FAIR. Use when setting up or repairing a package, checking one before submission, or drafting data, code, and materials availability statements. Adapted from Yusaku Horiuchi's replication-package-guide.

scdenney-open-science-skills-research-gr.description: Interviews a researcher in rounds until an idea, design, or draft has no unexamined decision — numbered questions, each with why it matters and a recommended answer, facts looked up rather than asked, and settled decisions written to a file. Stages are idea (topic or hunch to a falsifiable question and contribution claim), design (estimand, identification, sample and power, measurement, analysis plan, pre-registration, venue), and defend (reviewer objections to a finished design or draft). Use when the user says "grill me", asks to stress-test or poke holes in an idea, design, or plan, asks…
scdenney-open-science-skills-research-gr.tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, Agent, WebSearch, WebFetch, AskUserQuestion

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-resea.description: Interviews a researcher in rounds (idea, design, or defend stage) until no decision in a research idea, design, or draft is left assumed, recommending an answer to each question and writing settled decisions to a file. Use for 'grill me', stress-testing a design, or an idea not yet a design; --plan for software or process plans.

scdenney-open-science-skills-research-re.description: Scaffolds or audits a research-project repository organized around its source library (original PDFs, tracked Markdown conversions, drop zone, bibliography, intake pipeline) plus the analysis, manuscript, and review folders the project type needs. Use when starting, structuring, or auditing a research repo or its sources folder. Single-PDF intake goes to process-source, replication packages to replication-package.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-resea.description: Scaffold or audit a research-project repository organized around its source library (PDFs, Markdown conversions, bibliography, intake pipeline) plus the analysis, manuscript, and review folders it needs. Use when starting or auditing a research repo. Not for one-PDF intake or publication replication packages.

scdenney-open-science-skills-research-wa.description: Plans a research project as a decision map that persists across sessions, resolving one ticket per session until the design is defensible and pre-registerable. The map lives as Markdown in the repository, literature sweeps run as parallel research tickets, and the resolved map compiles into a pre-analysis plan. Use at project start, when a design has more open decisions than one conversation can hold, or when planning restarts each session. Not for executing analyses or writing the paper.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-resea.description: Plans a research project as a durable decision map, resolving one design decision per session until the design is defensible and pre-registerable. Use at project start, when a design has more open decisions than one conversation holds, or when planning keeps restarting. Not for running analyses or writing the paper.

scdenney-open-science-skills-sitrep.description: Start-of-session situational report for a research or code repository. Reads the handoff, log, or status files the project actually keeps, checks live git state, and reports the objective, verified baseline, open tasks, blockers, and next actions, flagging where the documents and the repository disagree. Use when resuming work after time away or before changing anything. Its end-of-session twin is finished.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-sitre.description: Start-of-session report on where a repository stands. Reads the project's own handoff and log files, checks live git state, and reports objective, verified baseline, open tasks, blockers, and next actions. Use when resuming work. Twin of finished.

scdenney-open-science-skills-archive-cod.description: Spawn full peer Codex or Claude sessions in their own panes and git worktrees — real sessions, not subagents — briefed by the lead and merged back. Not for bounded consults a subagent covers. Use when work must outlive or run beside this session, needs its own worktree, or must stay user-steerable.

scdenney-open-science-skills-archive-cla.description: Spawns full Claude Code peer sessions in separate terminal panes and git worktrees, real sessions rather than subagents, each with a directed task and contract brief, monitored and merged by the spawning lead. Detects the environment and uses herdr first, then tmux, then a native claude background agent. Use when work must persist or run beside the current session, needs a separate worktree or permission settings, should remain user-steerable in a visible pane, or when the user asks to spawn, hand off, or parallelize full sessions. Also spawns Codex peers into those panes. Excludes bounded…

scdenney-open-science-skills-survey-data.description: Audits fielded survey-response data for registered elements, data quality, bot and AI-automation screening, and sample integrity, and produces an appendix-ready quality report. Use at soft launch before full field, after fielding before outcomes are analyzed, or when asked what a study did about bots and AI respondents.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-surve.description: Audit fielded survey response data for registered elements, data quality, bot and AI-automation screening, and sample integrity, and emit an appendix-ready quality report. Use at soft launch or after fielding, before outcomes are analyzed.

scdenney-open-science-skills-survey-desi.description: Designs survey instruments, covering question wording, scale construction and index reliability, flow and treatment placement, pretesting and soft launches, respondent burden with attention and speeding rules, sensitive questions and social-desirability bias, and treatment delivery. Use when the user writes or revises survey questions, chooses a scale, orders blocks, plans a pilot, or worries respondents will not answer honestly. Indirect measurement goes to list-experiment, multi-country instruments to cross-national-design, and live-survey operations to qualtrics-ops.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-surve.description: Designs survey instruments: question wording, scales and index reliability, flow and treatment placement, pretesting, attention and speeding rules, and sensitive questions. Use when writing or revising survey questions, choosing scales, ordering blocks, or planning a pilot.

scdenney-open-science-skills-tables.description: Designs publication tables for social-science manuscripts. Covers whether a result belongs in a table at all, column order, row grouping and panels, decimal precision, standard-error and confidence-interval conventions, self-contained titles and notes, and code-generated output. Use when building or revising a regression, balance, descriptive, or robustness table, or when working with modelsummary, stargazer, gt, esttab, or booktabs. Finished tables go to figure-table-audit for end-stage QA.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-table.description: Design and format publication-quality tables. Use for column order, row grouping, notes, statistical precision, accessibility, and reproducibility.

scdenney-open-science-skills-text-classi.description: Advises on setting up LLM-based text classification as a validated measurement design. Covers codebook construction, learning-regime and model choice, prompt construction, validation against human coding with kappa and F1, hybrid human-LLM review, downstream measurement error, and reporting, plus a short resumable batch pattern with a rule-based baseline for repeated free text against a closed codebook. Use when the user wants to classify, code, or label text at scale. Category discovery goes to topic-modeling.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-text-.description: Advises on setting up and validating LLM text classification: codebook, learning regime and model choice, prompts, validation against human coding (kappa, F1), hybrid review, measurement error, and reporting, plus a short resumable batch pattern with a rule-based baseline. Use to classify, code, or label text at scale; category discovery goes to topic-modeling.

scdenney-open-science-skills-topic-model.description: Advises on setting up and validating topic models for survey and experimental text. Covers the discovery-versus-measurement question, choosing STM, LDA, or BERTopic, preprocessing consequences, prevalence and content formulas, topic-count selection across coherence, exclusivity and FREX, held-out likelihood, and residuals, validation of topics against human judgment, robustness, and DA-RT-compliant reporting. Use when the user has open-ended responses or another corpus and asks what topics are present, how many topics to use, about STM, searchK, coherence, or FREX, or wants topic prevalence…

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-topic.description: Advises on setting up and validating topic models for survey and experimental text: discovery vs. measurement, STM/LDA/BERTopic choice, preprocessing, covariate formulas, choosing K across coherence, FREX, held-out likelihood, and residuals, validating topics against human coding, robustness, and reporting. Coding against a fixed codebook goes to text-classification.

scdenney-open-science-skills-vlm-ocr.description: OCRs scanned or image-only corpora with vision-language models in four phases. Triage inventories the scans, identifies script and language, and shortlists models by script, hardware, and data constraints. Evaluate selects a system by measured CER or WER against ground truth, using born-digital twins, a second reader, and decision rules set in advance. Run builds the production pipeline. Clean removes model artifacts, audits what every cleaning rule deletes, corrects with rule-based and LLM passes, and records provenance. Use when choosing an OCR model for a corpus, measuring OCR accuracy,…

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-vlm-o.description: OCR scanned or image-only corpora with vision-language models in four phases: `triage` inventories the scans, identifies script and language, and shortlists models by script, hardware, and data constraints; `evaluate` picks a system by measured CER/WER against ground truth, using born-digital twins, a second reader, and decision rules set in advance; `run` builds the production pipeline; and `clean` removes model artifacts, audits what every cleaning rule deletes, corrects with rule-based and LLM passes, and records provenance. Born-digital documents with a text layer go to $doc-to-markdown;…

scdenney-open-science-skills-vlm-ocr-ali.description: Runs the GPU part of a vlm-ocr pipeline on Leiden University's ALICE cluster. Decides whether a corpus needs ALICE, picks a GPU partition for the model, sets up storage, a pinned vLLM environment and offline weights, ships code and scans, runs a gate job and chained bulk jobs with the bundled SLURM template, and brings the page records home for post-processing. Use with vlm-ocr when OCRing scans on ALICE or deciding whether to.

scdenney-open-science-skills-codex-vlm-o.description: Run the GPU part of a $vlm-ocr pipeline on Leiden University's ALICE cluster: decide whether a corpus needs ALICE, pick a GPU partition for the model, set up storage, a pinned vLLM environment and offline weights, ship code and scans, run a gate job and chained bulk jobs with the bundled SLURM template, and bring the page records home for post-processing. Use with $vlm-ocr when OCRing scans on ALICE or deciding whether to.
